name: PostgreSQL
tldr: PostgreSQL support for Prisma 8: config, runtime, contract authoring, and migrations in one package.
description: The one package a PostgreSQL application installs. It wires the SQL family, the PostgreSQL target, adapter, and driver into `defineConfig` and the `postgres()` runtime, and ships a `serverless` entrypoint for per-request runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers and AWS Lambda. Every other PostgreSQL extension plugs into this one.

name: MongoDB
tldr: MongoDB support for Prisma 8: config, runtime, contract authoring, BSON values, and migrations in one package.
description: The one package a MongoDB application installs. It provides `defineConfig`, the `mongo()` runtime with the ORM client and the typed pipeline builder, contract authoring, control-plane access, and BSON value constructors under `@prisma/orm-mongo/bson`.

name: SQLite
tldr: SQLite support for Prisma 8: config, runtime, contract authoring, and migrations in one package.
description: The one package a SQLite application installs. It wires the SQL family, the SQLite target, adapter, and driver into `defineConfig` and the `sqlite()` runtime, which opens the database file at the `path` you pass. Same contract, query builder, and migration model as PostgreSQL, so a project can start on a local file and move later.

name: pgvector
tldr: Vector columns and similarity search for embeddings.
description: Adds the pgvector `Vector(n)` column type, cosine and other distance operators, and vector indexes. Ships the migration that runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector`, so `db init` installs pgvector for you.

name: PostGIS
tldr: Geometry columns and geospatial queries such as distance and containment.
description: Stores points, lines, and polygons as a typed `Geometry` column with optional SRID, reads and writes them as GeoJSON-shaped values, and adds seven query operations: `distance`, `distanceSphere`, `dwithin`, `contains`, `within`, `intersects`, and `intersectsBbox`. Declares PostGIS as a database dependency so `db init` enables it.

name: ParadeDB
description: Registers the `bm25` index type so a contract can declare ParadeDB full-text search indexes through the standard index surface, and emits `CREATE INDEX ... USING bm25` DDL. Supports the `key_field` index option only so far.

name: Supabase
tldr: Supabase auth and storage tables plus role-bound clients for row-level security.
description: Ships a contract of every Supabase-managed `auth` and `storage` table and the `anon`, `authenticated`, and `service_role` roles, so your app can reference them without emitting migrations for them. The runtime adds `asUser(jwt)`, `asAnon()`, and `asServiceRole()` to bind the Postgres role and JWT claims per request.

name: arktype-json
tldr: JSON columns validated by an arktype schema and typed end to end.
description: Declare a `jsonb` column from an arktype `Type`. The emitted `contract.d.ts` renders the column as the schema's TypeScript shape, and the runtime validates every value it decodes against the same schema.

name: Cache middleware
tldr: Serve repeated reads from an in-memory or pluggable cache, opted in per query.
description: An opt-in caching middleware built on the `intercept` hook. Annotate a query with a TTL and identical plans are answered from the cache without touching the driver. Ships an in-memory LRU store and a `CacheStore` interface for Redis or other backends. Works on PostgreSQL and MongoDB runtimes.
